chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ibn Mahbub, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far عليه السلام: May I perform salat (prayer) while images are before me and I am looking at them? He said: "No. Cast a cloth over them. There is no problem with them if they are on your right, or your left, or behind you, or under your feet, or above your head. But if they are in the qiblah-direction, then cast a cloth over them and perform salat (prayer)."

key_terms.التَّمَاثِيلُ: images or statues present in the place of prayer
key_terms.ثَوْبًا: a cloth used to cover the images

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) if images or statues are in front of him?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about performing salat (prayer) in the presence of images. It states that images directly in front of the worshipper, especially in the qiblah-direction, should be covered, while their presence in other directions does not invalidate or obstruct the prayer.
